title: Theorem A
body_md:
{\em{\cite{Bieberbach-1916}}} If $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{U})$, then $|a_2|\leq 2$. Equality holds if, and
only if, $f$ is a rotation of the Koebe function.
head: environment

title: Bieberbach's conjecture
body_md: If $\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{U})$ and is given by \eqref{eq1}, then $|a_n|\leq n$ for any integer $n\geq 2$. Equality holds if and only if $f$ is a rotation of the Koebe function.
head: environment

title: Theorem B
body_md: {\em{\cite{Clunie-1960}}} Let $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{U})$ with $f(z) = z + \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n z^n$. If $\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} n \vert{}a_n\vert{} \leqslant 1,$ then $f \in \mathcal{S}^*(\mathbb{U})$.
head: environment

title: Theorem C
body_md: {\em{\cite{Nevanlinna-1920}}} The coefficients of each function $f\in\mathcal{S}^*(\mathbb{U})$ satisfy $|a_n|\leq n$ for $n=2,3,\ldots$. Strict inequality holds for all $n$ unless $f$ is a rotation of the Koebe function.
head: environment

title: Theorem D
body_md: {\em{\cite[Corollary, pp. 45]{Duren-1983}}} If $f\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{U})$, then $|a_n|\leq 1$ for $n=2,3,\ldots$. Strict inequality holds for all  $n$ unless $f$ is a rotation of the function $\mathcal{L}$ defined by $\mathcal{L}(z)=z(1-z)^{-1}$.
